<div class="eyebrow"><span class="eyebrow-mark"></span> SCHOLARSHIP & PROJECTS</div>

# Research<span class="accent-period">.</span> {.interior-title}

<p class="interior-lead">My work spans comparative and historical political economy and political methodology, with particular attention to institutions, state capacity, and the lasting effects of political conflict.</p>

::: {.hairline-section}
<div class="section-index">01 <span>/</span> WORKING PAPERS</div>

::: {.research-item}
<div class="item-index">2026 · HPE / STATE CAPACITY</div>

### Exams, Elites, and the Local State: Bureaucratic Incorporation and Territorial Governance in Joseon Korea

How does a centralized premodern state distribute resources across localities? This project examines whether access to the central civil bureaucracy was associated with where state relief was provided in Joseon Korea, using historical records of events and civil-service examinations.

<div class="research-meta">Working paper · SSRN preprint</div>
:::

::: {.research-item}
<div class="item-index">2026 · POLITICAL LEGACIES / KOREA</div>

### A Funeral Without End: The Political Legacy of the May 18 Democratization Movement in South Korea

Investigates how the 1980 Gwangju Democratization Movement shaped electoral politics over the long term, including political change after democratization and its geographic reach.

<div class="research-meta">Working paper · Supported by the May 18 Memorial Foundation</div>
:::

::: {.research-item}
<div class="item-index">2026 · POLITICAL METHODOLOGY / NLP</div>

### Across Languages and Political Contexts: Transfer Learning for Political Text Classification

Evaluates the transfer of political natural language inference models from English to Korean political text, focusing on cross-lingual transfer, local adaptation, and the challenges of domain-specific measurement.

<div class="research-meta">Working paper · SSRN preprint</div>
:::
:::

::: {.hairline-section}
<div class="section-index">02 <span>/</span> WORK IN PROGRESS</div>

::: {.research-item}
<div class="item-index">POLITICAL ECONOMY / HISTORICAL MEMORY</div>

### Boycotts and Ballots: Activated Memory, Political Consumerism, and Electoral Accountability under Trade

Studies how historical resistance and collective memory condition consumer behavior and electoral responses during international trade disputes, with a focus on the 2019 Korea–Japan trade conflict.

<div class="research-meta">Work in progress</div>
:::
:::

### We Made Participatory Budgeting: Political Science Beyond the Classroom

Woo Chang Kang, Sumin Kim, and Jong Rock Jeong, editors. *Bunny on the Moon*, 2025. ISBN 9791193671221.

<div class="research-meta">Edited book</div>
